title: Monday Morning Quarterback
date_line: Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. College Friday night review: Florida State at Pittsburgh, Illinois at UCLA and Houston at Colorado (Nov. 13), graded.

paragraphs: Friday put three college games on the board, and all three are final. Florida State won 16-10 at Pittsburgh, and the Pittsburgh −3.5 tickets died slowly. They were down 13-10 with the whole fourth quarter to play, got a Florida State fumble at the Pitt 12 and a targeting flag that moved them to midfield, and then a fourth-down sack at 8:44 ended the drive and the dream. The Under 54.5 was never in danger. The teams scored 26 points.
UCLA beat Illinois 22-14, and Illinois +10 cashed by 2 after a late field goal. Colorado beat Houston 42-32, and Colorado +10 cashed in a rout, while the Under 50.5 never had a chance.

Every game below is graded against the line printed on the card at kickoff, using ESPN finals and play-by-play, and a push counts as neither a hit nor a miss. Friday's Lock It Up line moves count at their final lines. The Cover Writer's card had Pittsburgh −3.5 and the Under 54.5, projecting Pittsburgh 31, Florida State 23; Illinois +10 and the Over 46.5, projecting UCLA 29, Illinois 20; and Colorado +10 and the Under 50.5, projecting Houston 28, Colorado 20.

Next Man Up and Letdown Watch rode Pittsburgh −3.5 too. The Formula and In The Trenches took Florida State +3.5 and cashed. On that total, the Cover Writer, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money had the Under, and Next Man Up and The Formula had the Over. The Formula had the Under on Monday and flipped on Friday's line move, which is the kind of move that keeps a gambler up at night. On the late games, the Cover Writer and The Formula cashed Illinois +10, and the Cover Writer and Follow The Money cashed Colorado +10 and Colorado +9. Next Man Up went 0-3 against the spread and 0-3 on totals Friday.

Card line: Pittsburgh −3.5, total 54.5. The Cover Writer's card had Pittsburgh −3.5 and the Under, projecting Pittsburgh 31, Florida State 23. Final: Florida State 16, Pittsburgh 10. Florida State won by 6, and the teams scored 26 points.

Pittsburgh −3.5 was the ticket that stayed alive just long enough to hurt. The Under 54.5 crowd, on the other hand, never broke a sweat. Florida State kicked field goals of 37 and 27 yards, Dailey found Turner for an 11-yard Pitt touchdown, and it was 7-6 Pitt at the half with 13 points on the board. Under holders were already counting money. Pitt holders were fine too: up one, needing a four-point win, with a whole half to get it.

Then the third quarter turned on Pitt. Kennedy picked off Dailey on Pitt's second snap of the half and set Florida State up at the Pitt 32, and Thomas plunged in from a yard out on the fifth play of the drive. Chadha's 34-yard field goal made it 13-10, and suddenly the math was simple for every Pittsburgh −3.5 ticket: one Pitt touchdown and the cover was back. Pitt then turned it over on downs at its own 42 with four seconds left in the third.

The fourth quarter handed Pitt holders two gifts. Daniels broke a 14-yard run and lost the ball at the Pitt 12, and Pitt recovered at its own 6. Three points stayed off the board, and the Pitt ticket still had a pulse. On the next drive, a targeting flag on Florida State turned a third-down incompletion into a Pitt first down at the Florida State 49. A touchdown from there makes it 17-13, a four-point win, and Pittsburgh −3.5 cashes by half a point. Instead, on fourth down at 8:44, LaVallee sacked Dailey at the Florida State 48 for a turnover on downs. Panikowski hit from 47 yards two minutes later, and at 16-10 even a Pitt touchdown could not cover anymore.

Pitt still got one last ride. Hughes punted 64 yards to the Pitt 2, Dailey ran for 24 and a roughing call moved Pitt to its own 46, and the last fourth-down throw fell incomplete at the Florida State 34 with 43 seconds left. Florida State won 16-10, so Pittsburgh −3.5 missed by 9.5 and the Under 54.5 stayed under by 28.5. The Formula had the Under on Monday, flipped to the Over 52.5 on Friday's line move, and watched 26 points go up. That one is self-inflicted.

Called it: The Formula and In The Trenches on Florida State +3.5, covered by 9.5 points. The Cover Writer and Letdown Watch on the Under 54.5, stayed under by 28.5 points. Follow The Money on the Under 52.5, stayed under by 26.5 points.

Missed: The Cover Writer, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on Pittsburgh −3.5, missed by 9.5 points. The Formula on the Over 52.5, fell 26.5 points short. Next Man Up on the Over 54.5, fell 28.5 points short.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side; In The Trenches on the total.

items.matchup: College Friday · Down to the wire

paragraphs: Card line: UCLA −10, total 46.5. The Cover Writer's card had Illinois +10 and the Over, projecting UCLA 29, Illinois 20. Final: Illinois 14, UCLA 22. UCLA won by 8, and the teams scored 36 points.

Illinois +10 hung on in the rain in Pasadena. Dieffenbach found Mizell for a 54-yard touchdown, and Bhaghani's 20-yard field goal made it 10-0 UCLA at the half. Gobaira sacked Houser in the end zone for a safety at 8:27 of the third, and UCLA led 12-0. Illinois +10 was still alive, and the Over 46.5 had 12 points on the board.

Houser found Feagin from 18 yards at 1:08 of the third, 12-7. Then Dieffenbach found Morgan for a 26-yard touchdown at 11:38 of the fourth, and it was 19-7. Illinois +10 was losing by two. Houser hit Dixon from 7 yards at 7:14, 19-14, and Illinois +10 was comfortable again.

Then Jackson intercepted Houser at the UCLA 40 and brought it back 41 yards to the Illinois 19. A UCLA touchdown there cashes UCLA −10. Bhaghani settled for a 37-yard field goal at 1:56. Illinois's last try ended on downs at 43 seconds. UCLA won 22-14, so Illinois +10 cashed by 2, and the Over 46.5 fell 10.5 short at 36.
Called it: The Cover Writer and The Formula on Illinois +10, covered by 2 points.
Missed: Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on UCLA −10, missed by 2 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Over 46.5, fell 10.5 points short.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total; In The Trenches on the side or the total.

items.matchup: College Friday · No sweat against the number

paragraphs: Card line: Houston −10, total 50.5. The Cover Writer's card had Colorado +10 and the Under, projecting Houston 28, Colorado 20. Final: Houston 32, Colorado 42. Colorado won by 10, and the teams scored 74 points.

Colorado +10 never needed the points. Houston led 20-7 after Dimas hit from 52 yards at 2:36 of the second. Taylor broke a 67-yard run at 1:49, and Smith's 32-yard run with 15 seconds left in the half put Colorado up 21-20. The Under 50.5 already had 41 points on the board at the half.

Houston's first snap of the second half was a sack and a fumble, and Colorado recovered. Williams caught a 53-yard touchdown on the next drive, and the Under 50.5 was finished. A 14-yard Colorado run at 5:26 of the third made it 35-20.

Houston's two-point try failed after a 22-yard touchdown at 10:00 of the fourth. Young scored from 2 yards at 3:59, and another two-point try failed after Walker's 4-yard touchdown at 1:51. Colorado won 42-32. Colorado +10 cashed by 20, and the Under 50.5 went over by 23.5.
Called it: The Cover Writer on Colorado +10, covered by 20 points. Follow The Money on Colorado +9, covered by 19 points. The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Over 50.5, cleared it by 23.5 points.
Missed: The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on Houston −10, missed by 20 points. The Cover Writer and Next Man Up on the Under 50.5, went over by 23.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the total; In The Trenches on the total.

hits.heading: Part 1, continued: The week's W-L and smack talk

paragraphs: The Cover Writer went 2-1 against the spread and 1-2 on totals Friday, and that runs the week to 7-4 against the spread and 5-6 on totals. Illinois +10 cashed by 2, and Colorado +10 cashed by 20. Pittsburgh −3.5 missed, and both late totals missed: the Over at UCLA and the Under at Colorado. A winning side card and a totals card that needs work.

The Formula went 2-1 against the spread and 1-2 on totals Friday, 6-5 and 5-6 for the week. Florida State +3.5 and Illinois +10 cashed. Then Houston −10 missed by 20, and the Over 52.5 at Pittsburgh is still the one that stings. Two wins on the side, and the totals card went the other way.

Next Man Up went 0-3 against the spread and 0-3 on totals Friday, 3-8 and 4-7 for the week. Pittsburgh −3.5, UCLA −10, Houston −10, and every total missed too. Still the worst side mark in the room, and the gap got wider.

Letdown Watch went 0-3 against the spread and 2-1 on totals Friday, 4-7 and 8-3 for the week. The three side tickets all missed, but the Under at Pittsburgh and the Over at Colorado cashed, and that totals mark is still the one everybody else is chasing.

Follow The Money went 1-0 against the spread and 1-0 on totals Friday, 2-1 and 3-1 for the week. It waited until Friday, took the Under 52.5 at Pittsburgh and Colorado +9 at the moved line, and cashed both. Patience pays, and it is not shy about saying so.

In The Trenches went 1-1 against the spread and made no total picks Friday, 3-4 for the week, still with no totals. Florida State +3.5 cashed, Houston −10 did not. Back below even, and the trenches are not done talking.
